channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: US teens are smoking and vaping less than their peers abroad
item.description: Lower youth smoking and vaping rates in the US deserve attention because they challenge the assumption that harm reduction for adults must come at the cost of youth protection. The real question is what policies, norms and enforcement patterns are helping to reduce adolescent use while still recognising that adult smokers need alternatives to cigarettes. Youth prevention and adult harm reduction should not be treated as opposing goals. A serious nicotine strategy has to protect young people without distorting the risk message for everyone else. (Published on August 20, 2026bytheconversation.com)

item.title: Tobacco: EU Commission consultation has closed
item.description: Transparency is not a procedural detail in EU tobacco policy; it is part of the evidence base. A consultation that is criticised as complex, steering or opaque risks weakening trust before legislation is even drafted. That matters especially in a debate where cigarettes, vapes, heated tobacco and nicotine pouches carry different risk profiles and require careful distinction. Europe’s next framework should be built through a process clear enough to support credible, proportionate regulation. (Published on August 21, 2026byeunews.it)

item.title: Tobacco sales continue to fall
item.description: New Zealand’s tobacco sales data points to a major long-term shift away from cigarettes. Sales volumes have fallen sharply, but the rise of cheap illegal tobacco shows why lower smoking rates cannot depend on enforcement alone. Smokers need legal, affordable and credible routes away from combustion, including accurate information about vaping as a lower-risk cessation tool. The next stage of tobacco control should protect progress by making the safer pathway easier than the illicit one. (Published on August 21, 2026bybeehive.govt.nz)

item.title: Nicotine nonsense
item.description: Nicotine policy often collapses into confusion because the central distinction is blurred. People smoke for nicotine, but they die mainly from the toxic products of combustion. Treating every nicotine product as though it carries the same risk as cigarettes makes public health advice less accurate and less useful. A clearer strategy would separate dependence from disease, protect young people and help adult smokers move away from the most harmful form of nicotine use. (Published on August 21, 2026bythecritic.co.uk)
